header: How a reader names a circular: the number the archive shows in its year list ("007"), together with the year, since serial numbers restart every January: "Circular 007 (2026)". I use the same three-digit padding as the circulars modal, and the same year rule as the upload (the year of the published date, which is what numbers the serial). The database's internal id is never shown to anyone.

members.name: query
doc: TypeORM's DataSource.query returns the rows themselves; node-postgres returns { rows }. I accept both.

symbols.name: circularLabel
symbols.sig: export function circularLabel(serial: number | null | undefined, year: number | null | undefined): string | null
doc: Returns "Circular 007 (2026)", or null when the serial or the year is not known (the caller then names the circular by its title).

symbols.name: fetchCircularLabels
symbols.sig: export async function fetchCircularLabels(db: QueryClient, ids: number[]): Promise<Map<number, string>>
doc: Maps circular id -> "Circular 007 (2026)". Ids with no serial are simply absent. It never throws: a failed lookup gives an empty map.

behaviours: id 49 -> 'Circular 007 (2026)' and id 51 -> 'Circular 008 (2026)' (what the 2026 list shows)
an older year keeps ITS year: id 7 -> 'Circular 005 (2022)' (the serial 5 of 2022, not the id 7)
a three-digit serial is not padded further: 'Circular 123 (2024)'
the YEAR RULE is the upload's (year of the published date): 31 Dec 2025 23:59 -> 2025, 1 Jan 2026 00:00 -> 2026
a circular with no serial number and an id that does not exist are simply absent (they will be named by title)
no empty list, duplicates or junk ids cause an error
works with TypeORM's return shape (an array of rows) as well
a failed lookup gives an EMPTY map (sources are then named by title), never an error
